statement.p: The figure below shows f(x) and its local linearization at x=a, y = 4 x - 4. (The local linearization is shown in blue.)

image.shortdescription: Graph of a concave up function and its tangent line at a point.

description.p: Graph of a concave up function and its local linearization. The two functions appear to intersect when x=4.

statement.p: What is the value of a?
What is the value of f(a)?
Use the linearization to approximate the value of f(4.2).
Is the approximation an under- or overestimate?

solution.p: Since the line meets the curve at x=4, we have a=4. Since the point with x=4 lies on both the line and the curve, we have f(a) = f(4) = 4(4) - 4 = 12. The approximation is an underestimate because the line lies under the curve. Since the linear function approximates f(x), we have f(4.2) \approx 4(4.2) - 4 = 12.8.
